title: Constructible dualizing composition mate and its coefficient equation
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0$ with $q$ elements and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], using its constructible exceptional adjunctions and finite-Tor categories $C_\Lambda(T)=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Integral operations are completed; field operations are the specified rationalizations and common finite-stage operations. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].
Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_Y:Y\to s$ and $a_X=a_Yf$. Write $\omega_{T,\Lambda}=Ra_{T,\Lambda}^!\Lambda_s$ for $T=X,Y$, with the coefficient unit and dualizing notation of [def-sf-pf]. Let $\alpha_\Lambda:Ra_{X,\Lambda!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{Y,\Lambda!}Rf_{\Lambda!}$ be the supplied (A4) compositor. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$c_{f,L}:Rf_\Lambda^!Ra_{Y,\Lambda}^!L\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X,\Lambda}^!L\qquad(L\in C_\Lambda(s))$$
whose postcomposition on $\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,-)$ is the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,Rf_\Lambda^!Ra_{Y,\Lambda}^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_{\Lambda!}K,Ra_{Y,\Lambda}^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_{Y,\Lambda!}Rf_{\Lambda!}K,L)\xrightarrow{h\mapsto h\circ\alpha_{\Lambda,K}}\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_{X,\Lambda!}K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,Ra_{X,\Lambda}^!L)$$
for every $K\in C_\Lambda(X)$; these are the (A1) Hom adjunction bijections with their pasted units and counits. In particular $c_{f,\Lambda}:=c_{f,\Lambda_s}$ is an isomorphism $Rf_\Lambda^!\omega_{Y,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,\Lambda}$.

For every allowed coefficient comparison of (A5), write $T_W:C_\Lambda(W)\to C_{\Lambda'}(W)$ for its functors, $u:T_s\Lambda_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda'_s$ for its unit comparison, and $\beta_h:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}Rh_\Lambda^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{\Lambda'}^!T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}$ for its exceptional comparisons. Define
$$\kappa_W=Ra_{W,\Lambda'}^!(u)\circ\beta_{a_W,\Lambda_s}:T_W\omega_{W,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{W,\Lambda'}.$$
Then the canonical mate satisfies the equality of morphisms in $C_{\Lambda'}(X)$
$$\kappa_X\circ T_X(c_{f,\Lambda})=c_{f,\Lambda'}\circ Rf_{\Lambda'}^!(\kappa_Y)\circ\beta_{f,\omega_{Y,\Lambda}}.$$
Allowed comparisons mean finite quotient and integral reduction where defined, and the scalar-extension, rationalization and common-stage comparisons specified in (A5); no reduction from field coefficients to finite coefficients is asserted. No ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility or biduality axiom is assumed.

proof.text: Write $F=Rf_{\Lambda!}$, $G=Ra_{Y,\Lambda!}$, $H=Ra_{X,\Lambda!}$ and $U=Rf_\Lambda^!$, $V=Ra_{Y,\Lambda}^!$, $W=Ra_{X,\Lambda}^!$, with counits $\epsilon_F,\epsilon_G,\epsilon_H$. All are functors between the specified constructible finite-Tor categories: the three adjunctions are precisely (A1), and $\alpha:H\xrightarrow{\sim}GF$ is (A4) of [def-sf-datum]. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], $GF\dashv UV$ has the composite Hom bijection and counit $e_L=\epsilon_{G,L}\circ G(\epsilon_{F,VL})$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] with $(L_1,R_1)=(GF,UV)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(H,W)$ and $\tau=\alpha$. It supplies a natural isomorphism $c:UV\xrightarrow{\sim}W$, the conjugate of $\alpha$; its inverse is the conjugate of $\alpha^{-1}$. This uses no exceptional right adjoint outside these categories.

source.place: Step 1: construct the composition mate using the supplied constructible adjunctions

proof.text:
The transpose description in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], specialized to identity vertical functors as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], gives
$$\epsilon_{H,L}\circ H(c_L)=e_L\circ\alpha_{UVL}.$$
For $t:K\to UVL$, naturality of $\alpha$ therefore gives
$$\epsilon_{H,L}\circ H(c_L\circ t)=e_L\circ GF(t)\circ\alpha_K.$$
Here $e_L\circ GF(t)$ is exactly the image of $t$ under the two inverse Hom adjunction bijections, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Applying the $H\dashv W$ Hom bijection proves the displayed Hom characterization in the item, including the direction $h\mapsto h\circ\alpha_K$. Any competing component $d_L$ with that action has $d_L=c_L$ by taking $K=UVL$ and $t=1_{UVL}$. Thus the natural isomorphism is unique. This is substitution into the cited component and Hom formulas, not an additional representability theorem.

source.place: Step 1: the Hom-chain normalization and uniqueness of the mate

proof.text:
Fix an allowed coefficient comparison and use primes for the target coefficient functors. Put $S=T_s$ and retain $T_X,T_Y$. The (A5) compatibility with (A1) and (A4) in [def-sf-datum] supplies compact-support comparisons
$$q_f:T_YF\xrightarrow{\sim}F'T_X,\quad q_g:SG\xrightarrow{\sim}G'T_Y,\quad q_x:SH\xrightarrow{\sim}H'T_X,$$
where $g=a_Y$, $x=a_X$. Set $Q=(G'q_f)\circ(q_gF):SGF\to G'F'T_X$. The compositor compatibility of (A5), written with the direction of $\alpha$ used here, is
$$Q\circ S\alpha=(\alpha'T_X)\circ q_x.$$
The adjunction compatibility of (A5) says that, for $h=f,g,x$ and $L$ in its target category,
$$\epsilon'_{h,T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}L}\circ F'_h(\beta_{h,L})=T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}(\epsilon_{h,L})\circ(q_h^{-1})_{U_hL}.$$
By the transpose characterization in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], this says exactly that $\beta_h$ is the mate of $q_h^{-1}:F'_hT_{\mathrm{source}(h)}\to T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}F_h$. We have only unpacked the assumed compatibility, not asserted a construction or existence of concrete coefficient comparisons. No $T$ from field coefficients to finite coefficients is used.

source.place: Step 3: write the (A5) compositor and adjunction compatibility squares

proof.text:
Take mates of the equality
$$S\alpha\circ q_x^{-1}=Q^{-1}\circ(\alpha'T_X):H'T_X\longrightarrow SGF,$$
which is the previous square with invertible sides rearranged. Use $GF\dashv UV$ as the source adjunction and $H'\dashv W'$ as the target adjunction, with vertical functors $T_X,S$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives the mate of $Q^{-1}$ under $GF\dashv UV$ and $G'F'\dashv U'V'$ as
$$B=(U'\beta_g)\circ(\beta_fV):T_XUV\longrightarrow U'V'S.$$
Clause (3b) of the same node, applied to the source transformation $\alpha:H\to GF$, identifies the mate of $S\alpha\circ q_x^{-1}$ as $\beta_x\circ T_Xc$. Clause (3a), applied to the target transformation $\alpha':H'\to G'F'$, identifies the mate of $Q^{-1}\circ(\alpha'T_X)$ as $(c'S)\circ B$. The mate correspondence is a function, so the equal left squares give equal right squares. Evaluating at $L\in C_\Lambda(s)$ yields
$$\beta_{x,L}\circ T_X(c_L)=c'_{SL}\circ U'(\beta_{g,L})\circ\beta_{f,VL}.$$
These are exactly the pasting and change-of-adjunction clauses stated in the cited node, with the vertical functors $T_X,S$ arbitrary; no full faithfulness or equivalence of coefficient functors is required.

source.place: Step 3: paste the coefficient mates and conjugate both sides of the composition square

proof.text:
Take $L=\Lambda_s$, put $J=S\Lambda_s$, and let $u:J\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda'_s$ be the supplied unit comparison. By [def-sf-pf], $V\Lambda_s=\omega_{Y,\Lambda}$ and $W\Lambda_s=\omega_{X,\Lambda}$. Postcompose the last equality by $W'(u)$. Naturality of the already constructed transformation $c':U'V'\to W'$ at $u$ gives
$$W'(u)\circ c'_J=c'_{\Lambda'_s}\circ U'V'(u).$$
Consequently the left side becomes $\kappa_X\circ T_X(c_{f,\Lambda})$, while the right side becomes
$$c_{f,\Lambda'}\circ U'\bigl(V'(u)\circ\beta_{g,\Lambda_s}\bigr)\circ\beta_{f,\omega_{Y,\Lambda}}=c_{f,\Lambda'}\circ Rf_{\Lambda'}^!(\kappa_Y)\circ\beta_{f,\omega_{Y,\Lambda}}.$$
This proves the claimed coefficient equation. Evaluation of the isomorphism $c$ at the coefficient unit also gives $Rf_\Lambda^!\omega_{Y,\Lambda}\cong\omega_{X,\Lambda}$. Each $\kappa$ is an isomorphism because it is the composite of a supplied comparison and the image of $u$ under a functor. Only naturality, functoriality and the displayed definitions are used in this last step.

Step 1: the conjugate of alpha:H->GF goes UV->W, using the composite counit eps_G.G(eps_F V) (matches Stacks 0DV0, categories.tex:3576). Step 2: the transpose is eps_H.H(c)=e.alpha_UV; naturality plus Yoneda give the Hom chain (h -> h.alpha_K) and uniqueness. Step 3: (A5) is unpacked as comparisons q_h with the compositor square and the counit square, so beta_h is the mate of q_h^{-1}; I checked all four corners. Step 4: clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting gives the mate of Q^{-1} as U'beta_g.beta_f V; clauses (3b) and (3a) give beta_x.T_X c and c'S.B; both mates are for the same adjunction pair, so they are equal. Step 5: postcomposing with W'(u) and using naturality of c' gives exactly the item's equation, which is the one the citer thm-sf-verdier-exchange step 4 uses (v=kappa_X, u=Rf'^!(kappa_Y).beta_f). Avoiding lem-sf-mate is justified: its statement assumes ambient admissibility, which def-fix-six-functor-datum (4) excludes. All the categorical nodes used are Mathlib leaves, so no tool_uses are needed. Edge cases checked: identity comparisons, f=id, empty X, field stages with no reduction to finite coefficients, arbitrary vertical functors. Searches record all three kinds. The concrete compositor nodes of the same unit and the trf/boundary dualizing-composition nodes are not duplicates.
